2025_070_m101425bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held October 14, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order at 7:00 p.m. by Vice President Anne with Trustee Philippart absent and adjourned at 8:06 p.m. The Board adopted resolutions recognizing Learning Disabilities Month, Principal Appreciation Month, and fifty-seven 2026 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, approved a four-item consent agenda, and issued a two-year probationary administrative contract to Saso Vasovski as Technology Director effective October 15, 2025. The largest financial action was the award of technology upgrade and access control bids totaling $2,698,071.79 as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund.
2025_070_m101425bdmtg.page:
Meeting and Attendance
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, October 14, 2025, held at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Vice President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present; Philippart was absent for all recorded votes. Superintendent Machesky attended along with administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Pagel, Zawislak, Cottone, Vasovski, and Trudel. Approximately 12 members of the audience were present. The meeting adjourned at 8:06 p.m. Minutes were submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (notation EA/jh).

Recognitions
The agenda opened with a TSD Mission Moment and presentation of the Apple Distinguished School Award to Troy Union Elementary and Larson Middle School, a designation held by fewer than a thousand schools worldwide.

Resolutions Adopted
- Learning Disabilities Awareness Month, October 2025: moved by Dr. Melton, supported by Mr. Haupt, noting that 1 in 5 individuals have a learning disability and joining Governor Gretchen Whitmer in commemorating October 2025 as Learning Disabilities Month in Michigan. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.
- Principal Appreciation Month: moved by Mrs. Zendler, supported by Mrs. Alic, recognizing October as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.
- 2026 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists: moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Zendler, honoring fifty-seven Troy students. More than one million students from some 21,000 high schools entered the program nationally and approximately 16,000 seniors were selected as semifinalists, by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT with comparable SAT scores. A reception was set for November 13th. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

Consent Agenda
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, approving items A through D: minutes of the September 2, 2025 Board Workshop; minutes of the September 16, 2025 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report for August 2025; and second reading and adoption of Board Policy Revisions. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

Personnel
Moved by Mrs. Potts, supported by Mr. Haupt, that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Saso Vasovski, beginning duties as Technology Director on October 15, 2025. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. There were no curriculum items.

Business
- Administration Building furniture purchase, not to exceed $300,000, through pre-existing bid contracts (consortiums), as an expenditure of the 2023 Bond Fund; moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Potts. Yes 6, No 0.
- Cafeteria tables for Barnard Elementary awarded to School Specialty in the amount of $46,937.22 from the 2023 Capital Projects Fund; moved by Mrs. Zendler, supported by Mrs. Potts. Yes 6, No 0.
- Technology upgrades and access control bids, moved by Dr. Melton, supported by Mrs. Potts, as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes 6, No 0.

| Vendor | Scope | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inacomp TSG | Structured Cabling | $77,464.32 |
| VSC | PA Systems & Emergency | 719,452.00 |
| Inacomp TSG | Classroom AV Systems | 245,974.65 |
| People Driven Technology | Access Control | 932,248.33 |
| People Driven Technology | Video Surveillance | 233,354.24 |
| People Driven Technology | Mandatory Alternate | 244,299.00 |
| Contingency (10%) | | $245,279.25 |
| TOTAL | | $2,698,071.79 |

Public Communication and Other Business
No additions, deletions, or agenda-item public comment. One community member addressed the Board during non-agenda public communication; no action was taken. Student representatives Chloe Gentilini (Troy College and Career High School), Ahyoung Song (International Academy-East), and Isabella (Bella) Doss (Troy High School) reported on school activities; Sara Graunstadt of Athens High School was absent. Board comments covered Diwali, Dr. Machesky's podcast "The Best is Yet to Come," homecoming parades, the MASB Annual Learning Conference, Disability Awareness Month, special education funding cuts and IDEA, the City of Troy bond ballot question for library, police and fire, and the closing of Central Office on November 1st for approximately 5 months. Mrs. Anne announced a Board Workshop on November 11th at 6:00 p.m. and the next regular meeting on November 18th at 7:00 p.m., both in the Services Building.
2025_070_m101425bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held October 14, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The minutes carry the notation EA/jh and are signed respectfully submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

CALL TO ORDER AND ATTENDANCE
Vice President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, Board members present were Alic, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Pagel, Zawislak, Cottone, Vasovski, and Trudel. There were approximately 12 members of the audience. Board member Philippart was recorded absent on every roll call vote of the evening.

RECOGNITION - TSD MISSION MOMENT / APPLE DISTINGUISHED SCHOOLS AWARD
The Board recognized two schools for earning designation as Apple Distinguished Schools, described as a recognition awarded to schools that are centers of innovation, leadership, and educational excellence, demonstrating a clear vision for learning with technology, a culture that supports continuous innovation, and compelling evidence of academic achievement and student engagement. Fewer than a thousand schools worldwide have earned the distinction. The Apple Distinguished School Award was presented to Troy Union Elementary and Larson Middle School, with congratulations to principals, staff, and students.

RECOGNITION - LEARNING DISABILITIES AWARENESS MONTH, OCTOBER 2025
The introduction noted that several national associations dedicated to supporting individuals with learning differences have designated October as a month of awareness, including organizations focused on Dyslexia, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), and Down Syndrome; that the U.S. Department of Education has recognized October as Learning Disabilities / Dyslexia / ADHD / Down Syndrome Awareness Month; and that Governor Whitmer declared October as Learning Disabilities Month in Michigan. It was moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mr. Haupt to adopt the resolution. The whereas clauses state that the term learning disabilities refers to differences in how brains work, which may affect the acquisition, organization, retention, understanding, or use of verbal or nonverbal information; that learning disabilities range in severity and may impact the acquisition and use of oral language, reading, written language, and mathematics; that 1 in 5 individuals have a learning disability; that learning disabilities may co-exist with other disabilities and conditions and can affect individuals regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, or other intersecting factors; that disabilities are a natural part of human diversity though individuals may face discrimination or marginalization; that every person has strengths; that specialized assessments and interventions involving home, school, community, and workplace settings can significantly enhance quality of life; that appropriate supports and services allow individuals to achieve their goals and participate fully in society; and that understanding and celebrating unique abilities is essential to an inclusive society embracing the strengths of all Michigan residents. The resolving clause has the Troy School District Board of Education join Governor Gretchen Whitmer in commemorating October 2025 as Learning Disabilities Month in Michigan. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Resolution adopted.

RECOGNITION - 2025 PRINCIPALS APPRECIATION MONTH
The introduction noted that October has traditionally been celebrated statewide as Principal Appreciation Month in recognition of building-level educational leaders. It was moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Alic. The whereas clauses cite that energetic and inspiring school leadership is essential if teachers, schools, and districts are to ensure all Troy students are college and career ready; that K-12 principals play a vital role in student success and act as liaison between school and community; that Troy School District principals are dedicated, quality educational professionals committed to sound leadership and guidance; and that the district joins educators, parents, and students throughout Michigan to raise awareness of educational leadership. The resolution officially recognizes October as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Resolution adopted.

RECOGNITION - 2026 NATIONAL MERIT SCHOLARSHIP SEMIFINALISTS
The narrative states that more than one million students nationwide from some 21,000 high schools entered the National Merit Scholarship Program and approximately 16,000 seniors were selected as semifinalists. Troy's fifty-seven semifinalists were named: Hasmita Anil Kumar, Fatima Ateeq, Matthew Batke, Shrish Bhandarkar, Mason Chiew, Sumehra Darafzin, Aarush Das, Arnav Dighrasker, William Dong, Lana Fargaly, Atul Ganesh, Vihaan Gehlaut, Aryan Goswami, Aaroosh Guduguntla, Anusha Gupta, Yeonjoon Ha, Kashifah Hossain, Aafla Ibraheem, Raghav Karur, Ryeo-Won Kim, Shlagha Kompelli, Aarush Kulkarni, Iniya Kumar, Ria Lattupalli, Phuong Le, Seungheon Lee, Sophia Li, Abigail Losey, Jing-Yi Ma, Jeeva Maridass, Joel Matthew, Aasrith Modem, Michael Molenda, Pratyush Neelakantan, Sameer Pai, Aayushi Parab, Kanghee Park, Sanjana Prabhu, Kristin Prakash, Akshiithi Prithiviraj, Tejaaswin Raja, Hansini Ramini, Sahas Ravoor, Ashwin Shrivastav, Divya Sovani, Chinmay Sujith Nair, Saanvi Thippireddy, Julia Triculescu, Yunis Turk, Matthew Vijayasegar, Akein Weerakoon, Anthony Wu, Casey Xin, Jonathan Xu, Alice Yang, Angela Zhang, and Eric Zhou. Copies of the resolution were to be presented to the students at a reception on November 13th. It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Zendler. The resolution notes that National Merit students reach semifinalist status by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test (PSAT) and earning comparable scores on the Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT). Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Resolution adopted.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS; PUBLIC COMMUNICATION ON AGENDA ITEMS
Both were recorded as None.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA
It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, and D on the consent agenda: minutes of the September 2, 2025 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the September 16, 2025 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report - August 2025; and Second Reading and Adoption - Board Policy Revisions. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

PERSONNEL - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, DIRECTOR OF TECHNOLOGY
It was moved by Mrs. Potts and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Board of Education issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Saso Vasovski, who will begin his duties as Technology Director on October 15, 2025. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

CURRICULUM
Recorded as None.

BUSINESS - ADMINISTRATION BUILDING FURNITURE PURCHASE
It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Potts that the furniture purchase for the Administration Building for an amount not to exceed $300,000 through pre-existing bid contracts (consortiums) be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Bond Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

BUSINESS - CAFETERIA TABLES, BARNARD ELEMENTARY
It was moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Potts that the purchase of cafeteria tables be awarded to School Specialty in the amount of $46,937.22 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

BUSINESS - TECHNOLOGY UPGRADES AND ACCESS CONTROL
It was moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mrs. Potts that the bid for technology upgrades and access controls be awarded as listed and approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Awards: Inacomp TSG, Structured Cabling, $77,464.32; VSC, PA Systems & Emergency, 719,452.00; Inacomp TSG, Classroom AV Systems, 245,974.65; People Driven Technology, Access Control, 932,248.33; People Driven Technology, Video Surveillance, 233,354.24; People Driven Technology, Mandatory Alternate, 244,299.00; Contingency (10%), $245,279.25. TOTAL $2,698,071.79. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS)
One community member addressed the Board during public communication. No action was taken by the Board.

OTHER
Recorded as None.

REPORTS FROM HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES
Chloe Gentilini, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Ahyoung Song, student representative for International Academy-East, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Sara Graunstadt, student representative for Athens High School, was absent. Isabella (Bella) Doss, student representative for Troy High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school.

BOARD COMMENTS
Board members congratulated Troy Union and Larson for receiving the Apple Distinguished Schools Award and mentioned: Happy Diwali to those who celebrate; Dr. Machesky's podcast "The Best is Yet to Come"; homecoming parades; the MASB Annual Learning Conference; Disability Awareness Month; special education program funding cuts and IDEA, with a plea for the community to reach out to senators and representatives; the upcoming election with a City of Troy bond for library, police and fire on the ballot; and that Central Office officially closed November 1st for approximately 5 months, with all future Board meetings to be held in the Services Building. Mrs. Anne announced that the next Board Workshop would be held in the Services Building on November 11th at 6:00 p.m. and the next regular meeting on November 18th in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m., and reminded everyone to vote at the upcoming election.

ADJOURNMENT
The meeting adjourned at 8:06 p.m.

2025_071_copy_november_board_update_2025.paragraph: A November 2025 Troy School District Board of Education presentation titled "Pieces of One Troy: Building Belonging Through Data and Action," reporting spring 2025 state assessment results for M-STEP, PSAT 8, and SAT 11 alongside Oakland County and statewide comparisons, subgroup performance gaps, and program celebrations. Troy's grades 3-7 M-STEP proficiency was reported at 67.9% in ELA and 77.9% in math for SY 25, against Oakland County figures of 49.8% and 55.4% and statewide figures of 38.9% and 42.7%. The presentation identifies special education as the largest and most persistent achievement gap and highlights third grade ranking first in the county in both ELA and math.
2025_071_copy_november_board_update_2025.page:
Purpose and Framing
Presented to the TSD Board of Education in November 2025 under the title "Pieces of One Troy: Building Belonging Through Data and Action." Stated purposes: student performance on state assessments and how performance has changed over time; district-by-district performance; performance gaps between student groups; and areas of focus and celebrations. The deck notes that state assessments are summative snapshots, one part of a balanced assessment system, useful to policy and decision makers for identifying schools, groups, and students for support, and are not designed to be diagnostic or drive day-to-day teaching and learning.

M-STEP Grades 3-7, Percent Advanced or Proficient

| 4 | 66.3 | 66.8 | 65.9 | 68.9 |
| 5 | 67.9 | 69.0 | 65.5 | 64.1 |

| 7 | 66.1 | 64.8 | 68.4 | 66.0 |

Grades 3-7 Proficiency Over Time

| Series | SY 19 | SY 22 | SY 23 | SY 24 | SY 25 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ELA TSD | 74.0% | 69.1% | 65.9% | 63.2% | 67.9% |
| ELA Oakland | 53.3% | 51.4% | 52.0% | 50.2% | 49.8% |
| ELA Statewide | 45.1% | 41.6% | 40.9% | 39.6% | 38.9% |
| Math TSD | 75.0% | 74.6% | 73.1% | 72.4% | 77.9% |
| Math Oakland | 57.3% | 53.6% | 54.8% | 55.9% | 55.4% |
| Math Statewide | 46.7% | 41.5% | 42.9% | 43.4% | 42.7% |

County comparison bars for grades 3-7 show 71%, 70%, 67%, 66%, 66%, and 62% in ELA and 71%, 70%, 68%, 68%, and 65% in math.

PSAT 8 and SAT 11
ELA: 84.2% grade 8 and 77.3% grade 11 in 2024; 83.5% and 79.3% in 2025. Math: 64.3% grade 8 and 59.5% grade 11 in 2024; 64.3% and 60.7% in 2025. Eighth grade ELA over time for TSD: 87.1%, 81.0%, 85.6%, 84.2%, 83.5% across SY 19 through SY 25, versus Oakland 72.5%, 69.5%, 71.4%, 74.4%, 74.5% and statewide 61.9%, 59.7%, 59.7%, 64.5%, 65.3%. Eighth grade math TSD: 75.1%, 67.5%, 69.1%, 64.3%, 64.3%; Oakland 55.1%, 47.6%, 49.0%, 45.9%, 42.4%; statewide 41.4%, 36.2%, 36.3%, 32.6%, 30.4%. Eleventh grade ELA TSD: 82.9%, 75.3%, 76.9%, 77.3%, 79.3%; math TSD: 73.6%, 61.6%, 61.3%, 59.5%, 60.7%.

M-STEP Science and Social Studies (Grades 5, 8, 11)
Science 2025: 61.1%, 65.3%, 50.2%; 2024: 62.6%, 64.4%, 46.3%. Social studies 2025: 51.0%, 68.1%, 56.9%; 2024: 34.9%, 47.5%, 46.6%.

Gap Analysis
The deck frames the performance gap, also called an opportunity gap, for students with disabilities, economically disadvantaged students, and English learners. Multi-Tiered System of Support actions include coherence building, Professional Learning Communities at all schools, universal supports, progress monitoring for students on a plan, a district handbook, interventions taught by content-strong teachers, and a focus on Tier 1 instruction. Special education is called the largest and most persistent achievement gap; economically disadvantaged students outperform state and county peers though fewer than half meet proficiency; English learners perform strongly against county and state peers with a gap remaining.

Celebrations
Third grade ranked first in the county in both ELA and math, with a spring 2025 third grade ELA proficiency chart topped at 67.9%. Troy Public Schools ranked fourth statewide with 108 Seals of Biliteracy in 2024-25. AP students scoring 3 or higher rose across five years to 89.0% in 2024-25, and AP English 11 enrollment reached 45.3% of eleventh graders in 2025-2026. Middle school honors math enrollment was reported at 22% of grades 6-8 in both 24/25 and 25/26.
2025_071_copy_november_board_update_2025.verbose:
Board presentation to the Troy School District Board of Education dated November 2025, titled "Pieces of One Troy: Building Belonging Through Data and Action." The stated purposes for the evening were student performance on state assessments and how performance has changed over time, district-by-district performance, performance gaps between student groups, and areas of focus and celebrations.

ABOUT THESE DATA
The deck explains that state assessments are summative assessments designed to be a snapshot in time of student performance; that they are one part of a balanced assessment system that uses multiple and varied assessments to provide all users with information they need to support teaching and learning; that they help policy makers and decision makers understand overall levels of achievement and identify schools, groups, and students for support; and that they are not designed to be diagnostic or drive day-to-day teaching and learning.

M-STEP GRADES 3-7, PERCENT ADVANCED OR PROFICIENT
ELA by grade (3, 4, 5, 6, 7), 2025: 67.9, 66.3, 67.9, 64.5, 66.1. ELA 2024: 63.2, 66.8, 69.0, 64.4, 64.8. Math 2025: 77.9, 65.9, 65.5, 65.8, 68.4. Math 2024: 72.4, 68.9, 64.1, 66.3, 66.0.

M-STEP 3-7 PROFICIENCY OVER TIME (SY 19, SY 22, SY 23, SY 24, SY 25)
ELA: TSD 74.0%, 69.1%, 65.9%, 63.2%, 67.9%; Oakland 53.3%, 51.4%, 52.0%, 50.2%, 49.8%; Statewide 45.1%, 41.6%, 40.9%, 39.6%, 38.9%. Math: TSD 75.0%, 74.6%, 73.1%, 72.4%, 77.9%; Oakland 57.3%, 53.6%, 54.8%, 55.9%, 55.4%; Statewide 46.7%, 41.5%, 42.9%, 43.4%, 42.7%. In both subjects the Troy line sits well above the Oakland County and statewide lines across every year shown.

M-STEP 3-7 COUNTY COMPARISON
The ELA grades 3-7 percent at or above proficiency bar chart displays district values of 71%, 70%, 67%, 66%, 66%, and 62%. The math grades 3-7 chart displays 71%, 70%, 68%, 68%, and 65%.

PSAT 8 / SAT 11 ELA AND MATH
ELA: grade 8 84.2% and grade 11 77.3% in 2024; grade 8 83.5% and grade 11 79.3% in 2025. Math: grade 8 64.3% and grade 11 59.5% in 2024; grade 8 64.3% and grade 11 60.7% in 2025.

EIGHTH GRADE PROFICIENCY OVER TIME (SY 19, SY 22, SY 23, SY 24, SY 25)
ELA: TSD 87.1%, 81.0%, 85.6%, 84.2%, 83.5%; Oakland 72.5%, 69.5%, 71.4%, 74.4%, 74.5%; Statewide 61.9%, 59.7%, 59.7%, 64.5%, 65.3%. Math: TSD 75.1%, 67.5%, 69.1%, 64.3%, 64.3%; Oakland 55.1%, 47.6%, 49.0%, 45.9%, 42.4%; Statewide 41.4%, 36.2%, 36.3%, 32.6%, 30.4%.

PSAT 8 COUNTY COMPARISON
ELA PSAT 8 percent at or above proficiency bars: 89%, 89%, 89%, 88%, 85%, 83%, 65%. Math PSAT 8 percent at or above proficiency bars: 70%, 64%, 64%, 63%, 60%, 30%.

ELEVENTH GRADE PROFICIENCY OVER TIME (SY 19, SY 22, SY 23, SY 24, SY 25)
ELA: TSD 82.9%, 75.3%, 76.9%, 77.3%, 79.3%; Oakland 63.1%, 59.5%, 59.5%, 60.0%, 64.1%; Statewide 55.3%, 51.6%, 52.2%, 51.3%, 55.4%. Math: TSD 73.6%, 61.6%, 61.3%, 59.5%, 60.7%; Oakland 46.5%, 39.4%, 39.1%, 35.6%, 37.4%; Statewide 36.3%, 30.0%, 29.9%, 26.3%, 27.5%.

SAT COUNTY COMPARISON
SAT Evidence Based Reading and Writing, grade 11 percent proficient: 85.1, 82.5, 82.3, 81.8, 79.3, 75.6, 55.4. SAT Math, grade 11 percent proficient: 64.7, 60.7, 58.9, 56.6, 56.5, 27.5.

M-STEP SCIENCE, GRADES 5, 8, AND 11
2025 percent advanced or proficient: 61.1%, 65.3%, 50.2%. 2024 percent advanced or proficient: 62.6%, 64.4%, 46.3%.

M-STEP SOCIAL STUDIES, GRADES 5, 8, AND 11
2025 percent advanced or proficient: 51.0%, 68.1%, 56.9%. 2024 percent advanced or proficient: 34.9%, 47.5%, 46.6%. All three grades show marked increases from the prior year.

GAP ANALYSIS - IMPLICATIONS AND ACTIONS
The deck states that historically districts have struggled to raise the performance of students with disabilities, economically disadvantaged students, and English learners on par with countywide and statewide rates of performance, commonly known as the performance gap, and that some refer to this as an opportunity gap wherein certain student groups have not been afforded adequate opportunities and support to perform on par with statewide and countywide peers.

MULTI-TIERED SYSTEM OF SUPPORT
Listed elements: district commitment to building coherence, in process; focus on systems that support all students; commitment to Professional Learning Communities, in process at all schools; universal supports; review of progress monitoring for any student on a plan; development of a district handbook; interventions taught by content strong teachers; and focus on Tier 1 instruction.

PERFORMANCE GAPS 2025 - SPECIAL EDUCATION
Values shown by Grade 3, Grade 5, Grade 6, Grade 7, Grade 8, and Grade 11. ELA special education: 45.4, 49.4, 47.7, 49.8, 52.3, 53.1. Math special education: 39.1, 40.9, 46.7, 49.3, 54.1, 51.7.

PERFORMANCE GAPS 2025 - ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED
Values shown by Grade 3, Grade 5, Grade 6, Grade 7, Grade 8, and Grade 11. ELA economically disadvantaged: 29.5, 24.2, 30.8, 27.2, 20.8, 25.7. Math economically disadvantaged: 22.6, 28.4, 32, 35.2, 41.4, 40.1.

ANALYSIS - STRENGTHS TO BUILD ON
TSD consistently outperforms county and state averages, demonstrating strong and effective instructional practices; all subgroups (economically disadvantaged, special education, English learners) are performing above their statewide peers, indicating effective support systems; performance stability over three years underscores the resilience and sustainability of current practices; and third grade ranked first in the county in ELA and math.

ANALYSIS - FOCUS AREAS FOR CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT
Special education represents the largest and most persistent achievement gap, with continued focus on inclusive practices and Tier 1 instruction and targeted interventions provided by content strong teachers. Economically disadvantaged students, while outperforming state and county peers, have fewer than half meeting proficiency and remain a critical area for support and targeted strategies and interventions. English learners show strong performance in comparison to county and state peers, yet a performance gap remains, and ongoing support for language acquisition and academic language development is described as essential.

MIDDLE SCHOOL MATH PERFORMANCE UPDATES
A cohort slide for the current 9th grade, Class of 2029, notes it is the last split cohort with a 6/7 and 7/8 track and IM 6/7, and the first cohort with choice after 7th grade of Honors Algebra 1; cohort performance figures shown are 65%, 63%, 68%, 68% and 62%, 65%, 66%, 65%, with accompanying counts 15, 13, 16, 11 and 23, 21, 18, 24. A cohort slide for the current 8th grade, Class of 2030, notes IM 6th and IM 7th, with performance figures 65%, 63%, 68%, 68% and counts 8, 26, 14, 23 and 13, 19, 13, 18.

MIDDLE SCHOOL HONORS MATH ENROLLMENT (2021-2022 through 2025-2026)
Percent of middle school students enrolled in Honors Algebra 1: 13.1%, 12.7%, 12.0%, 19.8%, 17.3%. Honors Geometry: 2.08%, 1.66%, 1.87%, 1.30%, 2.93%. Honors Algebra 2: 0.81%, 0.76%, 0.20%, 1.10%, 1.90%. Grades 6-8 combined: 21/22 16%, 22/23 15%, 23/24 14%, 24/25 22%, 25/26 22%. The slide states that middle school enrollment in high school honors math has increased by 6% over the last 5 years, representing an additional 175 middle school students annually in 24/25 and 25/26 who have enrolled in honors level math.

CELEBRATIONS - THIRD GRADE ELA AND MATH
A spring 2025 third grade ELA proficiency ranking chart lists district values of 67.9%, 66.6%, 65.6%, 63.1%, 61.6%, 61.5%, 58.6%, 54.1%, 51.3%, 50.5%, 48.7%, 48.4%, 48.1%, 47.3%, 45.9%, 44.9%, 42.7%, 41.6%, 40.6%, 39.6%, 38.9%, 37.0%, 34.8%, 33.8%, and 21.0%. Slides declare TSD third grade first in county in ELA and first in county in math.

CELEBRATIONS - 2024-25 SEAL OF BILITERACY
Counts by district: Detroit Public School Community District 162; Grand Rapids Public Schools 126; Portage Public Schools 112; Troy Public Schools 108; Forest Hills Public Schools 106; Lincoln Park, School District of the City of 99; Dearborn City School District 90; Utica Community Schools 70; West Ottawa Public Schools District 70; Hamtramck, School District of the City of 69. The deck explains the Seal of Biliteracy recognizes students who have achieved proficiency in English and at least one additional language and highlights strong communication skills, cultural awareness, and academic achievement. Reasons it matters: gives students a competitive edge for college admissions and scholarships; supports career readiness by validating bilingual skills valued in the global workforce; honors and celebrates the linguistic and cultural diversity of students; and encourages continued language learning and cultural competence.

CELEBRATIONS - AP ENROLLMENT AND PERFORMANCE
AP students scoring 3 or higher: 82.5% in 2020-21, 84.6% in 2021-22, 87.3% in 2022-23, 86.6% in 2023-24, and 89.0% in 2024-25. Percent of 11th grade students enrolled in AP English: 37.5% in 2021-2022, 32.3% in 2022-2023, 41.8% in 2023-2024, 41.5% in 2024-2025, and 45.3% in 2025-2026. AP English 11 student performance, percent scoring a 3 or higher with mean score by school year: 84.6% and 3.56 in 2020/2021; 84.1% and 3.68 in 2021/2022; 83.3% and 3.56 in 2022/2023; 74.7% and 3.42 in 2023/2024; 89.5% and 3.68 in 2024/2025.

OTHER SECTIONS
A slide covers International Baccalaureate Diploma acquisition. The closing credits note the presentation template was created by Slidesgo, including icons by Flaticon and infographics and images by Freepik, followed by a "Many Thanks / Questions?" slide.
